title: Oneida Language Immersion, Culture and Teaching
provider: Fanshawe College with the Oneida community
price: Tuition varies; see official program page
description: An accelerated Ontario college advanced diploma delivered fully online, focused on Onyota’a:ka language immersion, teaching and revitalization. Fanshawe lists a September 2027 intake and recommends prior language skills.
region: Oneida Nation of the Thames / Ontario / online
notice: Admission requires secondary-school eligibility and a Oneida-language pre-admission assessment. Fanshawe says regional availability may vary and particularly encourages Oneida community applications; it does not state this course is Indigenous-only. Confirm intake and fees with Fanshawe.

title: Pre-Health Sciences Certificate
price: Provider lists C$3,967.62 Year 1 tuition; subject to change
description: An Anishinabek Educational Institute one-year certificate to develop science, math, communication and health-sector preparation for further health sciences study. The provider describes online delivery.
notice: AEI lists OSSD-level requirements, potential funding and limited seats; check current admission rules, Indigenous eligibility, seat availability, costs and application dates with the provider before applying.

title: Post-secondary education support
provider: Walpole Island First Nation Education Department
description: Walpole Island First Nation members can review support for post-secondary tuition, textbooks, living expenses and related education costs.
notice: For eligible Walpole Island First Nation members. Confirm applications, funding limits and deadlines directly with the department.

title: Adult Learning Centre: secondary-school credits
provider: Walpole Island First Nation Education Department
description: Adult learners can explore secondary-school credit completion, including prior learning assessment and recognition, through the Education Department.
notice: The department describes programming for adults over 18. Ask about enrolment, dates, credit pathways and eligibility.

title: Anishinaabeg Kinomaagewgamig immersion school
description: Kindergarten to Grade 6 Anishinaabemowin immersion education with cultural, community and land-based learning opportunities.
notice: A community school, not a public drop-in course. Confirm admission, age and attendance requirements with the school.

title: Giyakiishchigewin employment and skills training
description: Community employment and training services include skill development, career guidance, job-readiness support and referrals to education opportunities.
notice: Check eligibility, availability and program registration; the source does not publish specific current course intakes.

title: BBK: Visiting Elders and Aanishinaabemowin language circle
description: An early-years and family program listing a language circle, Visiting Elders, playgroups and parenting-related learning supports.
notice: Community-based early-years services; ask staff about participation, schedules and consent protocols. Not an open public Elder booking.

title: Nin-Da-Waab-Jig Heritage Centre and natural heritage research
description: The Heritage Centre supports natural and cultural heritage preservation, environmental projects, research and land-claims archives.
notice: An official research centre; no public course or archive-access commitment is implied. Ask about learning visits and information-access conditions.

title: Standing Stone School
description: Community Junior Kindergarten to Grade 6 school offering the Ontario curriculum with a strong Oneida cultural component.
region: Oneida Nation of the Thames / Southwold, Ontario
notice: Confirm admission and school services directly; it is not a general public learning event.

title: Oneida Language & Cultural Centre: Learn Our Language
description: Browse community-developed Oneida language lessons, self-study activities, vocabulary and teaching resources.
region: Oneida Nation of the Thames / online
notice: Community-provided resources. Respect cultural permissions and warnings about images or voices of people who have passed on.

title: Oneida language and cultural learning videos
price: Public web resources; check individual access
description: An original-provider collection of short videos about Oneida language and everyday topics, including introductions and counting.
region: Oneida Nation of the Thames / online
notice: The original community site controls access and reuse. Videos are linked rather than copied or rehosted.

title: Oneida Master Speakers: recorded messages and language knowledge
description: Meet the language centre's Master Speakers and discover their provider-published recorded messages, pronunciation work and cultural stories.
region: Oneida Nation of the Thames / online
notice: The provider cautions that some recordings contain images and voices of people who are no longer living. Do not reuse recordings without permission.

title: Oneida Hunt Camp language vocabulary and videos
description: A Oneida-language study page with hunting, firewood and food-preparation vocabulary, audio resources and links to original-provider videos.
region: Oneida Nation of the Thames / online
notice: An educational language page, not a currently scheduled hunting camp. Respect original-source terms.

title: Indigenous Reclaim: living traditional teachings and sharing knowledge
provider: National Centre for Truth and Reconciliation
price: Education portal; access may require registration
description: An NCTR-hosted interview with Jonathan and Anna Adams about learning from Elders, hide tanning, land-based practices and sharing teachings.
notice: NCTR Education Portal; access or registration conditions apply. Respect participants' cultural knowledge and the original publisher's media rights.

title: Northern Survivors of Île-à-la-Crosse: strength, loss and resilience
provider: National Centre for Truth and Reconciliation
price: Education portal; access may require registration
description: A provider-published video series featuring Survivors discussing childhood, community, residential-school harms and resilience.
notice: Content advisory: Survivor testimony includes separation, trauma and loss. Follow NCTR portal access requirements.

title: Eugene Arcand: truth, survival, sports and healing
provider: National Centre for Truth and Reconciliation
description: A five-part NCTR-hosted public exhibit sharing Survivor Eugene Arcand's reflections on residential school, sport, healing and reconciliation.
notice: Content advisory: firsthand testimony discusses residential-school trauma. The original exhibit has its own credits and permissions.

title: Building Brighter Futures bursaries and scholarships
description: First Nations, Inuit and Métis students can review education funding and current application rules. Funding and deadlines depend on the award.
notice: Check program-specific eligibility, deadlines and proof requirements directly with Indspire.

title: Programs and courses
description: Explore Ogwehoweh languages, college programs, skilled trades and education pathways at Six Nations Polytechnic.
notice: Admissions and Indigenous-specific prerequisites vary by program.

title: Indigenous-centred degree programs
description: Browse Indigenous studies, languages, knowledge and science, health, education, social work and other degree pathways.
notice: Confirm admissions and location or distance options before applying.

title: Certificate in Reconciliation Studies
description: An 18-credit certificate covering residential school history, reconciliation and Indigenous resurgence, with online delivery options.
notice: Post-secondary program; verify admission criteria and current term deadlines.

title: Indigenous Canada
provider: University of Alberta Faculty of Native Studies
description: A 12-module course on Indigenous histories, contemporary perspectives, land and relations. The university currently advertises a free first-module preview.
notice: Do not assume the entire course or certificate remains free; check enrolment pricing.

title: Indigenous Engagement and Partnership Development
provider: University of Alberta / Braiding Knowledges Canada
price: Free preview; paid options may apply
description: A 12-module online course on ethical relationships, Indigenous governance, consultation and collaborative research.
notice: Check current platform access, enrolment and certificate charges.

title: Land Back online course
description: Seven modules on land dispossession, Indigenous resistance, consent and the Land Back movement.
notice: Previous knowledge of Indigenous histories is recommended by the provider.

title: Truth and Reconciliation Week education portal
provider: National Centre for Truth and Reconciliation
description: Year-round classroom video programming with Survivor voices and Indigenous educators, intended for Grades 1–12.
notice: Educator portal registration is required. Content may discuss residential school harms.

title: Residential School History and Survivors’ Stories
provider: National Centre for Truth and Reconciliation
description: Recorded Survivor testimony and discussion of residential school history presented through the NCTR education portal.
notice: Content advisory: firsthand accounts of residential school trauma. Respect speakers' terms of access and reuse.

title: Archives and Collections
provider: National Centre for Truth and Reconciliation
description: Explore the NCTR's public archive and guidance for accessing TRC-era records, Survivor statements and oral histories.
notice: Content advisory: residential-school records and Survivor testimony may be distressing. Public access does not authorize reuse; observe NCTR's archival and consent protocols.

title: Teaching Resource Centre
provider: National Centre for Collaboration in Indigenous Education
description: Indigenous-perspective lesson plans on land-based skills, Indigenous languages and classroom subjects, with supporting videos.
notice: Respect attribution and any knowledge-sharing restrictions stated by contributors.

title: FirstVoices language resources
description: Community-managed Indigenous language resources, including words, audio, phrases, songs and stories.
notice: Communities control content; some resources need permission or login.

title: Understanding Indigenous Perspectives
description: Learning modules on Indigenous worldviews, ways of knowing, representation, reconciliation and treaties.
notice: Developed as educator and learner resources; check individual resource guidance.

title: Educational tours and workshops
description: Southern Ontario First Nations history and culture programs, guided experiences and virtual learning options.
notice: Ask the centre about current programming, pricing and site access before booking.
